title: Signed completed adjunction frame of a formal plane equation
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $S$ a reduced finite-type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], pure of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension] and a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Let $\mathfrak m$ be a maximal ideal with residue field $k$, $A=S_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $R=\widehat A$ its maximal-ideal-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $K_A$ the stalk of the adjunction line of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction]. Fix a complete local $k$-algebra isomorphism $R\cong T/(f)$, where $T=k[[x,y]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $0\ne f\in(x,y)$, and $T/(f)$ is reduced. Let $J=(f)\subset T$ and $\bar f$ denote the class of $f$ in $J/J^2$. Duals mean $\operatorname{Hom}_R(-,R)$, and exterior powers are [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]; all scalar extensions use [def-weil-module-base-change].

The element $\bar f$ is a basis of $J/J^2$, and there is a canonical comparison
$$\Phi:K_A\otimes_A R\xrightarrow{\sim}(J/J^2)^\vee\otimes_R\bigwedge^2_R(R\,\mathrm dx\oplus R\,\mathrm dy).$$
There is a unique $R$-basis element $\eta$ of $K_A\otimes_A R$ with $\Phi(\eta)=-\bar f^\vee\otimes(\mathrm dx\wedge\mathrm dy)$.

For every field $L$ and $k$-algebra map $\theta:R\to L$ whose restriction to $A$ factors through a generic point in its smooth one-dimensional locus, put $M_L=\Omega^1_{A/k}\otimes_A L$, where Kähler differentials are [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Let $\widehat{\mathrm d}_A:R\to\Omega^1_{A/k}\otimes_A R$ be the unique continuous extension of the universal derivation, with extension and continuity as in [def-trf-completed-differential-extension]. Put $e_x=\widehat{\mathrm d}_A(x)\otimes1$, $e_y=\widehat{\mathrm d}_A(y)\otimes1$ in $M_L$, and put $a=\theta(f_x)$, $b=\theta(f_y)$, with the termwise formal partial derivatives of [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. If $(a,b)\ne(0,0)$, the sequence
$$0\longrightarrow L\xrightarrow{1\mapsto(a,b)}L^2\xrightarrow{(u,v)\mapsto u e_x+v e_y}M_L\longrightarrow0$$
is exact. Under the determinant convention that sends $v\in M_L$ to $\bar f^\vee\otimes((a\,\mathrm dx+b\,\mathrm dy)\wedge\widetilde v)$, its values at $e_x,e_y$ are respectively $b\Phi(\eta)$ and $-a\Phi(\eta)$. The algebraic generic smooth-locus identification $\gamma_L:K_A\otimes_A L\xrightarrow{\sim}M_L$ satisfies
$$\gamma_L(\eta\otimes1)=e_x/b\quad(b\ne0),\qquad\gamma_L(\eta\otimes1)=-e_y/a\quad(a\ne0).$$
Both fractions are nonzero whenever defined. No inverse of $f_x$ or $f_y$ in $R$ is assumed.

The comparisons $\Phi$ respect changes of algebraic local presentation and continuous changes between plane power-series presentations as above inducing the identity of $R$, and their identifications compose for any three presentations. For every such presentation the generic comparison above is the same algebraic smooth-locus map $\gamma_L$.

source.place: Tag 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci), with the preceding lemma-determinant wedge formula. Agent-formulated formal-completion and inverse-frame refinement; the tag itself does not assert this completion theorem.

proof.text: The one-element sequence $(f)$ is regular: in $k[[x,y]]$ the lowest nonzero total-degree homogeneous parts of two nonzero series multiply to a nonzero polynomial over the field $k$, so multiplication by $f\ne0$ is injective; and $f\in(x,y)$ makes $T/(f)\ne0$. In particular $\bar f$ generates $J/J^2$ freely: if $hf\in(f^2)$ then $hf=uf^2$ for some $u$, whence cancellation gives $h=uf$. Thus $R\to J/J^2$, $\bar h\mapsto hf\bmod f^2$, is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Use an algebraic local chart defining $K_A$ in [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction], with ambient dimension $m$ and regular-sequence length $m-1$. Its localization is a polynomial-local presentation at a $k$-rational maximal ideal, since the point has residue $k$. The field $k$ is perfect (in positive characteristic $t^p-a$ has a root for every $a\in k$). Apply [lem-trf-completed-conormal-determinant-comparison] with $d=1,n=2,c=1,g_1=f$. The remaining hypotheses are exactly reducedness, finite type, pure dimension, lci, rational residue field and reduced completion from the statement. This gives $\Phi$ and its normalized generic comparison. The exterior line has basis $w=\bar f^\vee\otimes(\mathrm dx\wedge\mathrm dy)$. Define $\eta=\Phi^{-1}(-w)$; it is a basis, and injectivity of $\Phi$ proves uniqueness.

source.place: Tags 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), relation-first wedge formula, and 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci); agent specialization of the existing completed comparison.

proof.text: The finite separable residue extension in [lem-trf-completion-kahler-differential-comparison] is here $k/k$, with the given coefficient section. Its assertion (i) supplies exactly the unique continuous derivation used in the statement. For any allowed $\theta:R\to L$, the generic normalization in [lem-trf-completed-conormal-determinant-comparison] gives the short exact formal conormal sequence with $M=M_L$ and coordinate images $e_x,e_y$. Its relation column is $(a,b)$ because $g_1=f$. This is the asserted sequence after identifying $L\bar f$ with $L$ by Step 1. In particular it holds under the stated nonzero-column hypothesis; no tensor-exactness assertion for an arbitrary nonflat map is being used.

source.place: Tags 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), relation-first wedge formula, and 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci); agent specialization of the existing completed comparison.

proof.text: Write $w_L=w\otimes1$ and $\delta:M_L\to\lambda_T\otimes_R L$ for the determinant comparison supplied in Step 2. Its displayed relation-first formula gives $\delta(e_x)=\bar f^\vee\otimes((a\,\mathrm dx+b\,\mathrm dy)\wedge\mathrm dx)=-bw_L=b\Phi_L(\eta_L)$ and $\delta(e_y)=aw_L=-a\Phi_L(\eta_L)$. This formula is independent of a lift, since adding a multiple of $(a,b)$ adds the wedge of that vector with itself, which is zero. Thus it is exactly the determinant convention in the item.

source.place: Tags 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), relation-first wedge formula, and 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci); agent specialization of the existing completed comparison.

proof.text: By the normalization identity $\gamma_L=\delta^{-1}\Phi_L$ in [lem-trf-completed-conormal-determinant-comparison], Step 4 gives $\delta(e_x/b)=\Phi_L(\eta_L)$ when $b\ne0$ and $\delta(-e_y/a)=\Phi_L(\eta_L)$ when $a\ne0$. Apply $\delta^{-1}$ to obtain the two formulas. The image of the basis $\eta_L$ under the isomorphism $\gamma_L$ is nonzero, proving both nonvanishing assertions. Where both denominators are nonzero the two fractions agree because $ae_x+be_y=0$. All divisions take place in $L$.

source.place: Tags 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), relation-first wedge formula, and 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci); agent specialization of the existing completed comparison.

proof.text: The algebraic and continuous formal presentation compatibilities and threefold composition law are part of [lem-trf-completed-conormal-determinant-comparison]. Apply them to the plane presentations. For each presentation its normalization identity is $\delta_T^{-1}\Phi_{T,L}=\gamma_L$ with the same algebraic smooth-locus identification; therefore the generic comparison proved above is that map for every presentation. This claims naturality of the comparisons, without asserting that the coordinate-dependent frames are identical.
